title: Eventual vanishing of an ideal-power map whose evaluation is zero
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\iota:\mathcal I\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_X$ a monomorphism of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with $\mathcal I$ quasi-coherent and of finite type [pqf-def-coherent]. Put $P_n=\mathcal I^n$ with inclusion $j_n:P_n\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_X$ and $P_0=\mathcal O_X$, using the recursive ideal powers of [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk]. Assume $X$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $\mathcal F$ be quasi-coherent. Let $U\subseteq X$ be open with $x\in U$ if and only if $\iota_x$ is surjective. Fix sections $1_n\in P_n(U)$ with $j_n(1_n)=1$ and maps $r_{nm}:P_m\to P_n$ for $n\le m$ with $j_n r_{nm}=j_m$. For every $n$ and $\varphi:P_n\to\mathcal F$ such that $\varphi_U(1_n)=0$, there are $m\ge n$ with $\varphi r_{nm}=0$.

proof.text: Choose a finite affine cover. On an affine member identify the ideal and module with their affine section modules, and P_n with the nth power of a finitely generated ideal J.

proof.text: For generators f_i of J, evaluation on D(f_i) is phi(f_i^n)/f_i^n. Vanishing and the localization zero criterion give a common k with phi(f_i^(n+k))=0 for all i. A sufficiently high degree monomial contains one of these pure powers, so phi vanishes on a higher ideal power. For the zero ideal take a positive power directly.
